content.text:
I read the structure region by region, starting from the top left.

**Bicyclic head group.** The ring atoms are N(Me)–C(=O)–N, with the N joined to a pyrrolidine CH2CH2CH2 chain that closes onto the CH at the ring fusion. From that fusion CH, a C(Ar)=CH–N(Me) segment completes the six-membered ring.
- Six-membered ring: N1(C)–C(=O)–N–C4a(H)–C(Ar)=CH, closing back to N1.
- The right-hand N bears CH2 (a), then CH2 (b), CH2 (c), then the CH (C4a).
- SMILES for this part: CN1C=C(Ar)C2CCCN2C1=O. The C2 fusion carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

**Aryl ring.** It carries two OMe groups and a CH2 attached to the piperazine; the carbon bearing the head group is para to that CH2. The ring is c1(head)cc(OC)c(CN...)c(OC)c1.

**Linker.** The CH2 leads to a piperazine N, through the piperazine to its other N, then CH2CH2 to piperidine C4. The piperidine N is attached to the isoindoline-1,3-dione at position 5.

**Imide end.** The isoindoline N carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group, drawn without stereo.

Assembled SMILES:
CN1C=C(c2cc(OC)c(CN3CCN(CCC4CCN(CC4)c4ccc5C(=O)N(C6CCC(=O)NC6=O)C(=O)c5c4)CC3)c(OC)c2)C2CCCN2C1=O

Checking the isoindoline: the ring N is attached to C(=O) and C(=O), and the aromatic carbon bearing the piperidine N sits at position 5. In the SMILES, c4ccc5C(=O)N(...)C(=O)c5c4 starts at c4 (the substituted carbon), then two CH, then c5 (a fusion carbon) bearing C(=O), which is attached to N. After the second C(=O) comes the other fusion carbon c5, then c4 (CH) closing to the substituted carbon. The substituted carbon is therefore adjacent to a CH that is adjacent to a fusion carbon, which is position 5.

SMILES: CN1C=C(c2cc(OC)c(CN3CCN(CCC4CCN(CC4)c4ccc5C(=O)N(C6CCC(=O)NC6=O)C(=O)c5c4)CC3)c(OC)c2)C2CCCN2C1=O
